name: ASIF BIN ANWAR
title: Managing Partner
intro: Asif Bin Anwar is the Managing Partner of Avon Chambers, a Lincoln's Inn Barrister and Advocate of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh with experience in litigation, arbitration, corporate and commercial law, and dispute resolution.
bio: Asif Bin Anwar is the Managing Partner of Avon Chambers, a Barrister of Lincoln's Inn, and an Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. He was called to the Bar of England and Wales by Lincoln's Inn in 2008, enrolled as an Advocate of the Bangladesh Bar Council in 2009, and subsequently enrolled to practise before the High Court Division in 2012 and the Appellate Division in 2024.

Mr. Anwar is an astute litigator and highly skilled in dispute management through Arbitration and Mediation. He has extensive experience in complex civil, commercial, corporate, criminal, writ, company and admiralty matters before the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, and is adept at handling multi-tier commercial and civil disputes. He also has considerable proficiency in International Commercial Arbitration and advises clients on complex legal, regulatory and commercial matters.

His practice encompasses Constitutional and Litigation matters, Corporate and Commercial Law, Arbitration and Mediation, Banking and Finance, Finance and Investment, Taxation, Property and Real Estate, Employment and Labour Law, Family Law, Intellectual Property, Telecommunications, Information Technology and other emerging areas of law. His experience includes advising on complex transactions, regulatory issues and disputes requiring a combination of legal, commercial and strategic considerations.

Mr. Anwar has held several senior positions in leading chambers. Before establishing Avon Chambers, he served as Head of Chambers at Grays Chambers from November 2013 to June 2020. He has also served as a Partner at Vertex Chambers, where he is currently Of Counsel, and previously held senior positions at Chowdhury & Ullah and Khaled H Chowdhury & Associates.

Alongside his legal practice, Mr. Anwar has contributed to legal scholarship and education. He has published articles in leading national newspapers, including The Daily Star, where his published work includes “Viability of Children’s Court.” Having previously taught law, he continues to contribute to legal education and occasionally delivers lectures as a guest faculty member at the London School of Legal Studies South and in distance-learning programmes associated with the University of London, BPP University and the University of the West of England.

Mr. Anwar has been recognised as a Top Corporate Lawyer by Asia Business Law Journal consecutively in 2024, 2025 and 2026. He has also received special mentions as a recommended lawyer in The Legal 500 for a number of years.

bio: Maeesha Dhusharima is a tri-qualified lawyer — an Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, a Barrister of Lincoln’s Inn, England, and a Solicitor of the Supreme Court of NSW, Australia. She brings over a decade of substantive experience spanning complex family, employment, commercial, corporate, and other matters of law, together with international training in mediation and arbitration, as well as significant exposure to litigation practice.

Alongside her legal practice, Maeesha has also contributed to academia as a Lecturer at Bangladeshi as well as British universities, enriching her professional insight with a strong foundation in legal education.

She is a resourceful legal advisor with a proven ability to anticipate and evaluate risks, safeguard clients’ interests, and deliver effective, timely results. Known for balancing problem-solving with practical strategies, Maeesha consistently ensures cost-efficient and results-driven solutions, even under rigid and competing deadlines.

In addition, she brings substantive, high-level expertise from her in-house roles. Her Counsel experience includes advising entities ranging from Bangladesh’s top university to a multi-national company, providing her with a unique and practical perspective on corporate governance, complex institutional challenges, and commercial strategy. This background allows her to offer strategic legal solutions that are both technically precise and commercially grounded.

Currently based in Australia, she supports the practice in various legal activities remotely as a Partner to offer strategic legal solutions that are both technically precise and commercially grounded.

intro: Kristi Keya Saha is an Advocate of the District and Sessions Court, Dhaka and a Barrister of the Honourable Society of Lincoln’s Inn, England & Wales, with more than 8 years of experience across litigation, dispute resolution, corporate and commercial law, M&A, banking and finance, power and energy, public-private partnerships and policy advocacy.
bio: Kristi Keya Saha is an Advocate of the District and Sessions Court, Dhaka and also called to the Bar of England and Wales as a Barrister-at-Law by the Honourable Society of Lincoln’s Inn, UK, with more than 8 years of experience in litigation, dispute resolution, corporate & commercial, merger & acquisition, banking & finance, power & energy, public-private partnerships, policy advocacy. She holds an LLB from the University of London and completed the Bar Professional Training Course at Northumbria University, Newcastle, UK.

Kristi has practised with leading international and domestic law firms, chambers, international development organizations and INGOs, advising multinational companies, investors, businesses and public-sector institutions across a range of sectors. Her practice focuses on cross-border mergers and acquisitions, corporate and commercial transactions, banking and finance, regulatory and compliance matters, corporate governance, infrastructure and power and energy projects, dispute resolution and litigation. She has advised international clients on complex cross-border transactions in Bangladesh, including M&A, legal and regulatory due diligence, corporate structuring, regulatory approvals and compliance. Her sector experience includes power and energy, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals and ready-made garments, among others.

Kristi has particular expertise in regulatory reform and digital transformation. As Legal and Policy Specialist on the USAID Feed the Future Bangladesh Improving Trade and Business Enabling Environment Project, she played a leading role in the digital transformation of Bangladesh’s business registration system. She advised the Office of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms and the Ministry of Commerce on the legal and regulatory framework for the new electronic business registration system, including the digitization and automation of corporate documentation, legislative reform, institutional change management and implementation. The initiative supported greater transparency and efficiency, reduced administrative burdens and facilitated business entry in Bangladesh.

Her contentious practice covers criminal, labour, commercial and civil litigation, arbitration, title and property disputes, writ petitions, criminal litigation, labour and intellectual property disputes. She advises on contractual, corporate and regulatory disputes, with a particular focus on strategic risk management, dispute prevention and enforcement.

He is currently an Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, reflecting his continued professional development and commitment to the legal profession. His combination of academic knowledge, courtroom experience, analytical ability, and practical understanding of legal procedures enables him to effectively address complex legal issues and provide comprehensive legal services.

Advocate Sajidul Islam is committed to maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, diligence, and ethical practice. name: A K M Mahmudul Hoque Alif
title: Associate
intro: Mr. A K M Mahmudul Hoque Alif is a Barrister of the Honourable Society of Lincoln’s Inn, with an internationally grounded legal education and a practice focused on complex civil, commercial, corporate, banking and financial disputes.
bio: Mr. A K M Mahmudul Hoque Alif is a Barrister of the Honourable Society of Lincoln’s Inn whose practice is centred on civil and commercial disputes, corporate and financial litigation, banking matters, dispute resolution and strategic legal advisory work.

Educated and professionally trained in the United Kingdom, Mr. Alif brings an international perspective to legal practice while maintaining a strong understanding of the commercial, institutional and practical realities of the Bangladeshi legal environment.

He obtained his LL.B. (Hons) from the University of the West of England, UK, before pursuing advanced postgraduate legal study through an LL.M. at City St George’s, University of London. He subsequently completed his Bar Vocational Studies (BVS) at City St George’s, University of London and was called to the Bar by the Honourable Society of Lincoln’s Inn.

Mr. Alif serves as Legal Advisor to the Bangladesh API Manufacturers and Intermediaries Association (BAIMA), representing 12 reputed companies in Bangladesh’s API sector. Through this role, he has contributed to legal, financial and policy-related initiatives involving key institutions, including Bangladesh Bank and the Ministry of Finance, strengthening his experience at the intersection of law, finance, regulatory affairs and institutional policy.

His interest in dispute resolution developed early in his legal career. While pursuing his undergraduate legal studies, he qualified as an Accredited Civil Commercial Mediator with ADR ODR International, giving him an early appreciation of the importance of resolving disputes not merely through confrontation, but through negotiation, commercial judgment and carefully structured solutions.
Today, his practice reflects that combination of advocacy and problem-solving.

Mr. Alif advises and represents clients in a broad range of civil, commercial, corporate, banking and financial disputes. His areas of practice include Civil and Commercial Corporate Litigation, Banking and Financial Litigation, Investment Banking Litigation, Company Matter Litigation, Artha Rin Disputes, Property and Inheritance Disputes, Family Disputes, Alternative Dispute Resolution, Civil Commercial Mediation and Arbitration.

His work also extends beyond conventional courtroom litigation. He is engaged in contract, instrument and policy drafting and vetting, institutional legal advisory work, and the formulation and analysis of policies concerning financial institutions and government institutions. He advises on disputes and transactions where legal considerations intersect with commercial strategy, banking structures, corporate decision-making and institutional policy.

A particular area of his professional interest lies in banking, finance and commercially sensitive disputes, where the legal issue often forms only one part of a broader financial or business problem. His approach is therefore focused not merely on identifying what the law provides, but on understanding the client's commercial position, evaluating the surrounding risks and developing a practical legal strategy.

Mr. Alif places significant emphasis on legal analysis, opinion writing, drafting, contractual interpretation, regulatory analysis, dispute strategy and negotiation. He approaches each matter with the view that effective legal representation requires clarity of thought, careful preparation and an understanding of the client's larger objective.

His training as both a Barrister and a Mediator has shaped a practice philosophy that recognises an important distinction: not every dispute needs to be prolonged, but every dispute needs to be properly understood. Where litigation is necessary, he believes in focused and determined advocacy. Where a commercially sensible resolution is possible, he places equal value on negotiation, mediation and strategic settlement.

This balanced approach enables him to work across contentious and advisory matters, particularly where disputes involve companies, banks, financial institutions, investors, property interests, contractual relationships or institutional decision-making.

At the centre of Mr. Alif’s practice is a commitment to making complex legal issues understandable to the people and institutions he represents. He believes that clients should not simply receive legal advice; they should understand the reasoning, risks and practical consequences behind it.

For him, the practice of law is ultimately about trust, preparation and responsibility. Whether dealing with a substantial commercial dispute, a financial institution, a corporate matter or an individual facing a deeply personal legal problem, he approaches every instruction with the same objective: to understand the matter thoroughly, protect the client's interests and pursue the most effective legal solution available.

bio: Mahir Chowdhury Abir is an Associate at Avon Chambers, where he has worked since July 2023, from the chambers' formative period. Working closely with Head of Chambers Barrister Asif Bin Anwar and other colleagues, he has contributed to more than 300 contentious and non-contentious legal matters. He joined the chambers as an Apprentice Lawyer and, following enrolment as an Advocate, has continued to develop a broad, disputes-led practice grounded in research, drafting, case preparation and commercially focused advice.

His litigation work spans civil and commercial disputes, constitutional and administrative law, writs and judicial review, banking and financial disputes, land and property matters, labour and employment, tax and customs, criminal complaints and proceedings, and family and personal law. His role commonly involves analysing the factual and legal issues that determine a dispute, developing case strategy with senior counsel and colleagues, reviewing evidence, preparing pleadings, affidavits and written submissions, advising on procedure and settlement, and supporting matters through contested proceedings.

Alongside disputes, Mahir maintains an active corporate and commercial advisory practice. He has worked on company formation and governance, regulatory compliance, shareholder arrangements, commercial operations, restructuring and risk, and the drafting, review and negotiation of service agreements, shareholder agreements, joint ventures, licensing arrangements, vendor contracts, confidentiality agreements, settlements and other commercial instruments. His entrepreneurial background gives him a practical appreciation of the commercial considerations that sit behind legal instructions.

Arbitration forms an important part of his developing disputes practice. In 2025, he served as Substitute Secretary in two ad hoc arbitral tribunals involving commercial, land and civil disputes, gaining practical exposure to arbitral procedure, tribunal administration and award-related work. He also works with U.S. attorneys at Rose Law Firm, Oregon on cross-border litigation and arbitration, supporting evidence analysis, legal research and drafting across jurisdictions.

Mahir holds an LL.B (Hons) from the University of London and a Master of Laws (LL.M) from Eastern University. At the University of London, he obtained an Upper Second Class degree, achieved a First Class result and Country Highest in Public Law, and received the Best Researcher Award twice. He has also built a distinguished record in competitive advocacy: Best Mooter at the Henry Dunant Memorial Moot in 2023, Best Mooter (All Over) at the Stetson International Environmental Moot in 2025, and Best Mooter at the 2025 Philip C. Jessup Bangladesh Rounds. He subsequently represented Bangladesh at the White & Case International Rounds of the Jessup in Washington, D.C.

Beyond practice, Mahir is a member of the Dhaka Bar Association and has contributed to advocacy training and public discussion on the profession. Eastern University invited him to conduct a session on oral advocacy strategies in 2025, and The Daily Star later featured his views on the responsible use and regulation of artificial intelligence in legal practice. His advocacy achievements have also received extensive national media coverage.

Whether working on a contested brief, a commercial arrangement or an arbitral matter, Mahir approaches the task as part of a team, with close attention to the record, the governing law and the client's practical objective. His practice is defined by breadth, rigorous preparation and a research-led approach to resolving complex legal problems.

bio: Nazifa Sarwar is a Barrister and Advocate practising in Dhaka, with contentious and advisory experience in Bangladesh and England. She regularly appears before the District and Sessions Judge Courts of Dhaka and is developing a broad court-facing practice spanning commercial and corporate disputes, banking and Artha Rin matters, civil and property litigation, employment, family and custody proceedings, criminal and regulatory disputes, animal welfare matters, arbitration and contractual advisory work.

Her commercial and corporate practice includes disputes arising from contracts, business relationships, company affairs, insolvency and regulatory issues. She drafts pleadings, applications, written submissions, witness-related materials and legal opinions, reviews complex documentary and evidentiary records, and assists with case theory, hearing preparation and settlement strategy. Her UK experience also included a cross-border intellectual property and FinTech dispute involving a blockchain gaming company, crypto-assets, jurisdictional issues and tracing of international transactions.

Nazifa has experience in banking disputes involving loan facilities, recovery proceedings, repayment and rescheduling arrangements, settlement terms and contested CIB classification. Her Artha Rin work includes reviewing facility documents, sanction letters, repayment records, banking correspondence and settlement arrangements to identify substantive and procedural issues affecting recovery and defence strategies.

Her civil, property and land practice includes title and ownership disputes, possession claims, chains of title, title deeds, Heba deeds, succession documents, inheritance claims and competing interests in property. In England, she successfully represented parties in County Court civil and commercial hearings; in one possession matter, a Defence and Counterclaim she prepared identified a defective section 21 notice, after which the possession claim was dismissed.

Her employment practice includes contentious and advisory matters. In England, she appeared in an Employment Tribunal hearing at short notice and successfully argued an application to amend the claimant’s ET1 to introduce further allegations despite opposition, following which the respondent offered to settle through ACAS. She has also advised on settlement agreements and contractual employment issues.

Nazifa has conducted divorce proceedings and is familiar with complex child-custody disputes, including matters requiring careful handling of sensitive family evidence, competing parental positions and practical welfare considerations. Her prior family-law exposure in England included work and observation relating to family proceedings and financial-remedy issues.

Her criminal and regulatory practice is expanding to include contested animal welfare disputes. She is presently acting in an animal welfare matter involving the interaction of general penal provisions, animal-welfare legislation, police complaint/FIR procedure, evidentiary preservation and criminal complaint strategy, and is preparing to represent the client before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court in Dhaka.

Nazifa has also worked on commercial arbitration and adjudication matters. Her experience includes research, drafting, contractual and evidentiary analysis under ICC, SIAC and UNCITRAL frameworks, as well as supporting counsel in three concurrent construction adjudications involving urgent referral notices, witness statements, conferences and hearing bundles.

Before returning to Bangladesh, Nazifa worked at DWF Law LLP, Witan Solicitors and Quartz Barristers in England. At DWF she worked on a substantial insurer-litigation caseload, analysed evidence across more than 150 files, drafted defences, witness statements and applications, negotiated settlements and advised insurer clients on prospects and risk. She completed the LLM Barristers Training Course at Nottingham Trent University and is an Accredited International Civil and Commercial Mediator with ADR ODR International.

intro: Farha Binte Azad Etu is an Associate with experience in civil and commercial litigation, company matters, family matters, criminal litigation and arbitration.
bio: Farha Binte Azad Etu is an Associate with experience in civil and commercial litigation, company matters, family matters, criminal litigation and arbitration.
She has experience handling litigation matters from initial drafting through final disposal, with particular exposure to company matters, family disputes and writ proceedings.

In Pure Cotton Ltd v Perfect Fit Co. Ltd, she represented The Perfect Fit Co. Limited (Respondent No. 1 & 3) in Company Matter No. 1187 of 2024, handling the case end-to-end from drafting the Affidavit-in-Opposition through final disposal. The matter concerned an application for winding up under section 241(vi) of the Companies Act 1994. In its judgment dated 20 October 2025, the Court dismissed the winding-up application in full, holding that fraud is not an independent ground for winding up under Bangladeshi law, that the petitioner failed to establish contingent creditor status, and that the alleged debt was bona fide disputed.

In Shat-el-Ilias v Bangladesh & Others, she worked on the matter from start to finish concerning a Writ Petition for physical custody of two minor sons following the Family Court's visitation order in Family Suit No. 240 of 2026. The core issue before the High Court was whether writ jurisdiction should be invoked to interfere in custody, guardianship and visitation matters ordinarily reserved for the Family Court. In its judgment dated 17 May 2026, the Court discharged the Rule Nisi, holding that the petitioner had an equally efficacious remedy before the Family Appeal Court and that the Family Court remained the appropriate forum, while directing continuation of the existing visitation order and completion of the Family Court trial within two months.

bio: Eshrat Jahan is a Barrister of England and Wales with three years of experience in legal practice. She obtained her Bachelor of Laws from the University of London and subsequently completed the Barrister Training Course (BTC) alongside a Master’s degree at BPP University, London, UK.

Eshrat joined Avon Chambers in July 2024, where she has developed a diverse and rapidly expanding litigation practice within a relatively short period. Her professional experience spans approximately three years of legal practice, encompassing civil and commercial litigation. She also maintains an active family law practice, advising and representing clients in complex and sensitive matters, including divorce, child custody, and guardianship proceedings.

In addition to her civil and family law practice, Eshrat has experience handling complex land vetting and criminal matters, including bail and anticipatory bail applications. Prior to joining Avon Chambers, she worked with various law firms, gaining valuable practical exposure to a broad range of legal matters, including land vetting, family disputes, company law, and criminal proceedings. She is recognised for her analytical mindset, attention to detail, and commitment to continuous professional development.

Alongside her legal career, Eshrat serves as a Lecturer at British Study Academy (BSA), where she teaches Criminal Law, Contract Law, Tort Law, Company Law, and Property Law. Her teaching experience has further enhanced her ability to explain complex legal principles clearly, confidently, and effectively.

Eshrat is also actively involved in academic and advocacy-related activities. On numerous occasions, she has participated as a judge in Mooting Competitions at London College of Legal Studies (LCLS) South, where she has assessed students’ advocacy skills, legal reasoning, presentation, and ability to construct persuasive legal arguments.
